content.title: About
content.content: Shirley Temple is a non‑alcoholic cocktail named after the famous American child actress of the 1930s. It is made from ginger ale (or lemonade), grenadine and is garnished with a maraschino cherry. The drink has a bright red color and a sweet‑tart flavor, often served at children’s parties and family restaurants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink first appeared in the United States in the 1930s as a “kid’s cocktail”.
It was named after Shirley Temple after the actress tried it in a café and liked it.
Traditional recipes use ginger ale, but some versions substitute lemonade or sparkling water.
Grenadine gives the characteristic red hue and a subtle fruit note.
In some countries the drink is served with a slice of pineapple or lime instead of a cherry.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Grenadine, made from pomegranate juice, provides vitamin C which supports the immune system.

items.title: Controlled sugar content
items.content: When prepared at home you can limit added sugar, making the drink less sweet.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The sparkling water or ginger ale helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Pomegranate juice is rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Soothing ginger effect
items.content: Ginger ale may ease mild stomach discomfort.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Commercial versions often contain a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and tooth decay.

items.title: Pomegranate allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to pomegranate, an ingredient of grenadine.

items.title: Carbonated beverages
items.content: Large amounts of carbonated drinks can cause stomach discomfort in sensitive people.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Acidic components (lemon juice, grenadine) may irritate the mucosa if consumed excessively.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Shirley Temple chilled in a tall glass with ice, a splash of grenadine, a maraschino cherry and, optionally, a lime wedge. For a homemade version mix ginger ale, grenadine and lemon juice in a 3:1:0.5 ratio.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared drink in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Keep the individual ingredients (ginger ale, grenadine) in sealed containers away from light.
